Yes. Although I can't give you any sited sources, just my experience running a simulator in a research lab for 3 years. People's sense organs take in a lot more information that the brain is constantly filtering out and leaves at the subconscious level. Most of the time this information isn't important. But when it is absent it causes problems for the brain. We call this simulator sickness. While in the simulator, the brain takes in highly realistic visual, auditory, and tactile (sometimes we'd even add common perfumes or essential oils to add olfactory sensation). But when test subjects go around a corner some people will still get nauseous from the lack of acceleration and equilibrium sensory data going into the brain, when the brain is expecting that data.

Photographs transfer even less data than the simulator experience. Our monitors transmitted a lot of visual data and were more accurate and precise than most pictures. However, some photographs, depending on how they were taken and processed would transmit more visual data than the best simulator setups. This may not stay true going forward however.

tl;dr: pictures only supply a small amount of information and the human mind craves input from many sensory imputs, even when it doesn't use it most of the time.
